title: Oxtail Stew
subtitle: Slow-braised oxtail in red wine and root vegetables
excerpt: Oxtail sections braised for hours in red wine and stock with root vegetables until the meat falls from the bone in sticky, richly gelatinous pieces. A dish that rewards patience with one of the most intensely flavoured things a pot can produce.

recipe.sourceNotes: Oxtail stew is found in British, Italian (coda alla vaccinara), Jamaican, and West African cooking, among many other traditions. Oxtail was historically cheap and considered unfashionable offal; it is now recognised as one of the finest braising cuts because of its high collagen content. The collagen in the bones, cartilage, and connective tissue dissolves during the long, slow braise into gelatin, which gives the sauce its extraordinary body and glossy texture. Oxtail must be browned very thoroughly before braising for maximum flavour in the sauce. The dish is best made a day ahead: after refrigerating overnight the fat solidifies on the surface and can be lifted off, leaving a cleaner, more concentrated sauce.

content.text: Brown the oxtail sections in very small batches over the highest possible heat; crowding the pan makes them steam and they will not colour properly. The fat that renders out can be poured off between batches. Make this a day ahead if possible: the overnight rest in the fridge allows you to remove the fat and improves the depth of flavour.

items.preparation: use oxtail sections, about 1.5 kg; excess fat trimmed

content.text: Pat the oxtail dry and season very generously. Heat the oil in a large, heavy casserole over the highest heat. Brown the oxtail in 2 to 3 batches for 3 to 4 minutes per batch until deeply coloured on all sides. Remove and set aside.

Pour off most of the fat from the pan, leaving about 2 tablespoons. Cook the onion, carrot, and celery over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, tomato puree, and herbs. Cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine, scraping up the browned bits. Cook for 3 minutes. Add the stock and tinned tomatoes. Return the oxtail.

Bring to a simmer. Cover and braise in the oven at 150°C / fan 130°C / gas 2 for 3.5 to 4 hours until the meat is completely tender and falling from the bone. Remove the oxtail. Strain the sauce into a clean pan and reduce if needed until glossy and coating. Return the oxtail. Serve over mashed potato or polenta.
